title: Opening the Club Plantation floor shows under S. H. Dudley
summary: The band opens with a producer, chorus girls and acts, plays soft sweet music and learns patrons' favorite songs, with Charles cueing the shows.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: We finished that summer up and they brought the band in St. Louis to start rehearsing the floor show to open at the Club Plantation. There was a gentleman named S. D. Dudley Buttley, a showman and a show producer, who was producing the show. Back in those days we always had a line of girls, eight girls, chorus girls and comedians, always would bring in a dance team and we'd bring in some outstanding singer for the floor show.
And each floor show would last starting there two weeks, was it two weeks?

MR. PILLARS: Three weeks. And the third week we'd have to start rehearsing for a new show. That's where my brother, I used to depend on him because on opening nights of the show I'd have so many cues and things, I'd be kind of nervous and jerky and he was always calm and he would always tell me my cues. It was so-and-so next, so-and-so next.

And he was a great help to me. We opened the Club Plantation and to the best of my knowledge they had never had a band, a black band, to play like we played in St. Louis at that particular time. We played sweet music sweeter. And we played jazz, we played it, we played all varieties of music. And we did our best to keep the music soft, so the people in the nightclub could converse and enjoy themselves. This was where I learned from Gordon C. Harrison in Texarkana, Texas.

A few years before that. And, one thing we did started from our opening night, if we got a request for a piece if -- we knew it we'd play it and we kept a file of different tunes and -- that different friends would come in and like. And once we knew a person and knew the song they liked, they would never have to ask for that song anymore, because when they'd walk down the steps coming into that club, we would start playing their favorite song. Now this is what helped put the band over.
